title: Exercise the daemon Origin guard from the real client path
description: Objective: stop the control-room client from setting a header the browser will never send, and prove the daemon Origin guard against the real client path. Register item 8 of 11 from task-963cf1d125134c6193b7af0e53deeac3 (2026-08-14 product audit; verified real, classified low). RE-MEASURED STILL OPEN at HEAD 192360e: packages/control-room-client/src/client-transport.ts:90 `headersFor` returns an object including `origin: options.origin` (:93), which is then passed as `headers` to fetch at :108-111. `Origin` is a FORBIDDEN header name in the fetch spec - a browser silently drops it and sets its own - so this header is inert in the only environment that matters, while a non-browser fetch (tests, Node) sends it and satisfies the daemon guard artificially. The result is that the daemon Origin guard is exercised only by the vite proxy, and the real client path is never tested against it. Deliverable: stop setting the forbidden header, and cover the daemon guard with a test that drives the real client transport rather than a proxy-shaped fixture. NOT in scope: changing the daemon's Origin policy itself, the CSRF token scheme, the session credential header, or the wire protocol version header - only the forbidden header and the coverage gap. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test.
definitionOfDone: The client transport no longer sets the forbidden `origin` request header; a test asserts the exact header name set is what the client intends, so re-adding it fails rather than passing silently.

The daemon Origin guard is exercised by a test that drives the REAL client transport path, not the vite proxy and not a hand-built request that happens to carry an Origin - the coverage gap is the defect, so closing it is the deliverable.
A request that the daemon's Origin guard rejects is asserted by its exact stable reason code and refusing layer, not merely as a non-200.
The request URL still uses options.origin as its prefix (client-transport.ts:108) - only the HEADER is removed, and existing CSRF, session-credential and protocol-version headers are unchanged.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test exits 0.
taskRails: Do not relax the daemon Origin guard to make a test pass; the guard is correct and the client is what is wrong.
Do not hand-set an Origin header in the test to satisfy the guard - that reproduces the exact illusion this task exists to remove.

packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts is marked GENERATED - DO NOT EDIT BY HAND, source of truth @moe/contracts. If the change reaches generated output, report blocked and name a contracts/codegen task.

implementationPlan.description: Establish what the daemon actually requires, and pin it, before changing the client. apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-guards.ts:127 is `if (request.headers.origin !== origin) return "LISTENER_ORIGIN_INVALID";`, where the expected value comes from originOf(host, port) at :66 and the code is a member of the frozen list at :28. So the guard demands an EXACT match and refuses when the header is ABSENT, since undefined !== origin. apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener.test.ts ALREADY references LISTENER_ORIGIN_INVALID, so EXTEND that existing coverage rather than starting fresh: confirm it pins all three arms by exact code - matching Origin admitted, mismatched Origin refused, and NO Origin header refused - and add whichever arm is missing. This step changes no production code; it makes the daemon's contract explicit so the client change can be judged against it.

Guard ORDER matters: host is checked FIRST (:126), so an Origin arm must carry a valid Host or an earlier guard answers.

implementationPlan.description: Remove the forbidden header from the client. packages/control-room-client/src/client-transport.ts:90-96 headersFor returns an object containing `origin: options.origin`, passed as `headers` to fetch at :108-111. `Origin` is a FORBIDDEN header name in the fetch spec: a browser silently drops it and substitutes its own, so this entry is inert in the only environment that matters. Delete that one entry. Leave the other headers untouched - content-type, x-moe-csrf, x-moe-protocol-version, x-moe-session-credential - and leave the URL construction at :108 alone, since it uses options.origin as the request PREFIX and that use is correct and unrelated. In packages/control-room-client/src/client-transport.test.ts assert the EXACT set of header names headersFor produces, so re-adding `origin` fails loudly rather than passing silently.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD order held: the exact-header-set assertion was written and run RED first, for the right reason — the failure diff was literally `+ "origin",` inside the sorted key list — then the production entry was deleted.

Test added to client-transport.test.ts: `it("sets the EXACT header set it intends, and no forbidden header among them")`. It asserts the WHOLE sorted key set from the captured fetch init — ["content-type","x-moe-csrf","x-moe-protocol-version","x-moe-session-credential"] — not a subset, so re-adding `origin` (or any other header) fails loudly instead of passing silently. Also pins `not.toHaveProperty("origin")` and re-asserts the URL is `${ORIGIN}/command`, since the URL prefix is a SEPARATE use of options.origin that must survive.

Removed the stale `expect(call?.headers["origin"]).toBe(ORIGIN)` from the credential test — it asserted the defect.

Production change is exactly one line: client-transport.ts headersFor no longer emits `origin: options.origin`. content-type, x-moe-csrf, x-moe-protocol-version, x-moe-session-credential untouched; `${options.origin}${path}` at the fetch call untouched; TransportOptions.origin still required and still used.

Verified: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test → 6 files, 41 passed. pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client typecheck → exit 0. Generated client untouched. client-transport.ts now 137 lines (grep -c '').

implementationPlan.description: STATE AND HANDLE THE CONSEQUENCE - this is the part a careless fix gets wrong. In a BROWSER, removing the header changes nothing: it was being dropped anyway and the browser supplies Origin itself. In NODE it changes everything: no Origin header is sent, so the daemon's guard sees undefined and refuses every request with LISTENER_ORIGIN_INVALID. The transport supports non-browser use through options.fetch, so this is a real behavior change, not a theoretical one. Decide it explicitly and record the decision in a comment on headersFor: a non-browser caller must supply Origin through its own fetch wrapper, exactly as a browser does, because the transport cannot set it. Do NOT reintroduce the header behind an environment check, and do NOT relax the daemon guard to admit a missing Origin - task rail 1 forbids the latter and the former merely restores the illusion.
implementationPlan.note:
The consequence is stated in the code, not left as a footnote.

DECISION RECORDED on headersFor: `Origin` is deliberately absent, and so is the fallout. In a browser nothing changes — the header was being dropped and replaced anyway. In Node everything changes: no Origin is sent, the daemon sees undefined and refuses with LISTENER_ORIGIN_INVALID. That refusal is the HONEST answer, not a regression, and a non-browser caller closes it by supplying Origin through its own options.fetch wrapper, exactly as a browser does — because this layer cannot.

Explicitly written into the comment as forbidden: reintroducing the header behind an environment check (restores the illusion) and relaxing the daemon guard (task rail 1). Neither was done.

Second touch: the TransportOptions.fetch doc said only "Injected for tests; production uses the ambient fetch", which is now incomplete — options.fetch is the ONLY seam through which a non-browser caller can supply Origin, so it points at headersFor for the reason. Without that pointer the next reader hits the Node refusal and re-adds the header.

Comment-only step; no behavior changed. pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client typecheck exit 0; test 6 files / 41 passed. client-transport.ts is 158 physical lines by grep -c '' — under the 250 target.

implementationPlan.description: Close the coverage gap the item is really about, in the one place that can. Neither package can import the other - apps/daemon does not depend on @moe/control-room-client and the client depends only on @moe/contracts - so an end-to-end test belongs in tests/integration/control-room/control-room-transport.test.ts, which already drives createControlRoomTransport. Extend it so a REAL transport instance talks to a REAL daemon listener and the Origin the daemon sees comes from the fetch layer the way a browser supplies it, NOT from headersFor. Assert three arms by exact code: a correct Origin is admitted; a mismatched Origin refuses with LISTENER_ORIGIN_INVALID; and a request with no Origin at all refuses with the same code. Do NOT hand-set an Origin inside headersFor to make this pass - that reproduces exactly the illusion this task exists to remove, and it is the single most likely wrong turn here.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REMOVING THE HEADER vs FEATURE-DETECTING. Keeping the header for non-browser callers behind an environment check was considered and rejected: it restores the exact illusion the item is about - tests and Node clients would keep satisfying the guard by a route no browser can take, so the guard would remain untested from the real path while looking covered. CHOSEN: remove it unconditionally and require non-browser callers to supply Origin through their own fetch wrapper, which is what a browser does anyway.

RELAXING THE DAEMON GUARD WAS REJECTED OUTRIGHT and is written into the task rails. The guard is correct; the client is what is wrong. Admitting a missing Origin would turn a coverage gap into a security regression.

WHERE THE END-TO-END TEST LIVES. A daemon-side test would be the natural place and is impossible without a new workspace dependency on the client, which the dependency-edge rail forbids adding casually and which would invert the architecture. CHOSEN: extend the existing integration test, which already drives the real transport and sits outside both packages.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS PROMOTED TO ITS OWN STEP rather than left as a footnote, because it is the difference between a correct fix and a broken one: removing the header genuinely changes Node behavior from admitted to refused, and a worker who does not notice will either ship a broken non-browser client or quietly re-add the header when a test fails.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
RE-MEASURED AT HEAD 192360e; I raised this slice from the audit register at the same HEAD.

THE CLIENT SIDE. packages/control-room-client/src/client-transport.ts:90-96 headersFor returns { "content-type", origin: options.origin, "x-moe-csrf", "x-moe-protocol-version", "x-moe-session-credential" }, passed as `headers` to fetch at :108-111. `Origin` is a forbidden header name per the fetch spec, so a browser drops it and sets its own; a Node fetch sends it verbatim.

THE DAEMON SIDE. apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-guards.ts:127 `if (request.headers.origin !== origin) return "LISTENER_ORIGIN_INVALID";`, expected value from originOf(host, port) at :66, code declared in the frozen list at :28. Exact match required, and ABSENCE refuses too because undefined !== origin.

PUT TOGETHER, THIS IS WHY THE GUARD IS UNTESTED FROM THE REAL PATH: in a browser the client's header never arrives and the browser's own Origin decides the outcome; in Node the client's header arrives and satisfies the guard artificially. Neither case exercises the guard against what a real browser client actually sends.

EXISTING COVERAGE, MEASURED: apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener.test.ts is the file that already references LISTENER_ORIGIN_INVALID - there is no http-listener-guards.test.ts, so step 1 extends existing coverage rather than creating a file. On the client side packages/control-room-client/src/client-transport.test.ts exists.

NO DEPENDENCY EDGE EXISTS IN EITHER DIRECTION. apps/daemon/package.json declares contracts, coordination, core, mcp, review, runner, scheduler, store - NOT control-room-client. packages/control-room-client declares only @moe/contracts. So a daemon-side test cannot import the client and a client-side test cannot start the daemon; under the global dependency-edge rail neither edge may be added just to host a test. The end-to-end home is tests/integration/control-room/control-room-transport.test.ts, which ALREADY imports createControlRoomTransport - confirmed by grep - so the seam this task needs is already established there.

SIZE: client-transport.ts is 138 physical lines, ample headroom.
planningNotes.risks:
THE FIX BREAKS NON-BROWSER CALLERS, BY DESIGN, AND THAT MUST BE DELIBERATE. After removal a Node caller sends no Origin, the daemon sees undefined, and every request refuses with LISTENER_ORIGIN_INVALID. That is the honest consequence of removing a header a browser would never send - but if it is discovered as a surprise mid-implementation, the tempting repair is to put the header back, which undoes the task.

THE MOST LIKELY WRONG TURN is hand-setting an Origin inside headersFor, or inside the integration test, to make the guard pass. That reproduces precisely the artificial satisfaction this task removes. The Origin must reach the daemon from the fetch layer, as a browser supplies it.

THE VITE DEV PROXY MAY DEPEND ON CURRENT BEHAVIOR. The audit noted the daemon guard is satisfied only by the proxy today. Check the proxy configuration before concluding the dev path still works; a fix that leaves the dev setup refusing every request will be reverted rather than debugged.
